- PCGEditor.PCGEditorSubsystem: Editor scripting operations for building, inspecting and executing PCG graphs
- UMGEditor.UMGDebuggerSubsystem: Debugs UMG at runtime. The widget lifetime log records every user widget constructed,
destructed, rebuilt or invalidated while PIE runs, filterable by name, class, event type
and player, and the same recording can be opened in the Widget Lifetime Log editor tab.
Load this when investigating which widgets are created, rebuilt or torn down in PIE.
Widget Blueprint authoring lives in WidgetBlueprintEditorSubsystem.
- UMGEditor.WidgetBlueprintEditorSubsystem: Creates and edits UMG Widget Blueprints: builds and rearranges the widget tree,
manages named slots and UI components, wraps and replaces widgets, and compiles.
Load this when working with UMG / Widget Blueprint (UserWidget-based) UI assets.
- SequencerScripting.MovieSceneConditionExtensions: Manages runtime evaluation conditions on movie scene sections, tracks, and track rows.
Conditions are returned as editable objects. Setters create a new instance and respect the editor's condition class restrictions.
- SequencerScripting.MovieSceneEventTrackExtensions: Function library containing methods that should be hoisted onto UMovieSceneEventTrack for scripting
- SequencerScripting.MovieSceneFolderExtensions: Organizes movie scene folders, their display names, colors and sorting orders, and their child folders, tracks, and object bindings.
Null inputs and inaccessible assets raise script errors. Child folders and tracks must belong to the same movie scene as the folder.
- SequencerScripting.MovieSceneTrackExtensions: Creates, lists, and removes sections owned by movie scene tracks.
Section operations reject invalid inputs and inaccessible assets; transactions are caller-owned.
- SequencerScripting.MovieScenePropertyTrackExtensions: Function library containing methods that should be hoisted onto UMovieScenePropertyTrack for scripting
- SequencerScripting.MovieSceneBindingTagExtensions: Extension methods for reading and writing Sequencer binding tags.

Binding tags are name-based labels attached to object bindings in a
Sequence. They are authored interactively via RMB -> Expose on a binding
in the Sequencer editor, and queried at runtime via
UMovieSceneSequence::FindBindingByTag. These extensions expose the
authoring operations that are otherwise only available through the
editor UI.
Null sequences, empty tag names, and inaccessible assets raise script
errors. Binding proxies address IDs in their sequence's root space.
- SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSectionExtensions: Reads and edits section channels, keys, ranges and evaluation settings. Range frames use the owning movie scene's
display rate; pre-roll and post-roll use its tick resolution. Bound changes use its playback range;
transactions are caller-owned.
- SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSectionEasingExtensions: Function library containing easing methods that should be hoisted onto UMovieSceneSections for scripting
- SequencerScripting.MovieSceneSequenceExtensions: Reads and edits sequence tracks, bindings, root folders, frame rates and playback bounds.
Playback frames use the sequence display rate with an inclusive start and exclusive end.
Timing changes do not wait for pose evaluation. Selected tools obey the owning asset's
editor access policy; writes also respect scene read-only state.
- SequencerScripting.MovieSceneBindingExtensions: Function library containing methods that should be hoisted onto FMovieSceneBindingProxies for scripting
- SequencerScripting.MovieSceneFloatVectorTrackExtensions: Function library containing methods that should be hoisted onto UMovieSceneFloatVectorTrack for scripting.
A float vector track created from script has no channel count; set it before adding a section.
Null inputs and inaccessible assets raise script errors.
- SequencerScripting.MovieSceneDoubleVectorTrackExtensions: Function library containing methods that should be hoisted onto UMovieSceneDoubleVectorTrack for scripting.
A double vector track created from script has no channel count; set it before adding a section.
Null inputs and inaccessible assets raise script errors.
- SequencerScripting.MovieSceneTimeWarpExtensions: Function library containing methods that relate to time-warp within Sequencer
- SequencerScriptingEditor.SequencerToolsFunctionLibrary: This is a set of helper functions to access various parts of the Sequencer API via Python. Because Sequencer itself is not suitable for exposing, most functionality
gets wrapped by UObjects that have an easier API to work with. This UObject provides access to these wrapper UObjects where needed.
- SequencerAnimTools.SequencerAnimToolsEditorLibrary: Scripting for the Sequencer animation tools: motion trails, Time Posing and the Edit Pivot tool. Python: unreal.SequencerAnimToolsLibrary.
Every function raises a script error with the reason when it cannot do what was asked.
Functions that take a LevelSequence need it open and focused in the level editor's Sequencer.
Motion trail pin, space and offset functions need trails visible (SetMotionTrailsVisible); trail ids change whenever trails are
rebuilt (hidden and shown again, or a Sequencer opens or closes), so read them again with GetPinnedMotionTrails.
Frame parameters are display-rate frames unless TimeUnit is TickResolution.
- DataflowEditor.DataflowScriptingSubsystem: Builds, edits and inspects Dataflow graphs (UDataflow), standalone or embedded in an asset (e.g. a cloth asset).

A Dataflow asset contains a main graph, sub-graphs and variables. Graphs contain nodes linked through pins.
Graphs, nodes and pins are addressed by path:
- Graph: "" for the main graph, the sub-graph name otherwise
- Node:  "NodeName" in the main graph, "SubGraphName/NodeName" in a sub-graph; NodeName is the node's name, not its display name
- Pin:   "<NodePath>.PinName", e.g. "StaticMeshImport.Collection"

Node types are identifiers from ListNodeTypes: registered node types (e.g. "FAddFloatsDataflowNode"),
"SubGraph/<Name>" for a node running a sub-graph, and "Variable/<Name>" for a node reading a variable.
Data types are the Dataflow type names pins show, e.g. "float", "FVector", "TObjectPtr<UStaticMesh>", "TArray<int32>".
Values are in Unreal text export format, e.g. "1.5", "(X=1.0,Y=0.0,Z=0.0)" or "(1,2,3)" for an array.

Every change is one undo step. Errors raise, with a message starting with "[Code:Argument]". Assets are not saved.

Every function is both PythonCallable and an MCP tool (AICallable), registered with the toolset registry when it is loaded.
- ToolsetRegistry.AgentSkillToolset: Provides tools for listing, reading, and creating/updating skills.
- AIAssistantEditor.AIAssistantToolset: These functions help the AI assistant inspect its state as it relates to the larger Unreal Editor.
- SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers: Editor source control common functionality.
Functions tagged AICallable are also exposed over MCP as the toolset "SourceControl.SourceControlHelpers".

@note Many of these source control methods use *smart* file strings which can be one of:
  - fully qualified path
  - relative path
  - long package name
  - asset path
  - export text path (often stored on clipboard)

  For example:
     - D:\Epic\Dev-Ent\Projects\Python3rdBP\Content\Mannequin\Animations\ThirdPersonIdle.uasset
     - Content\Mannequin\Animations\ThirdPersonIdle.uasset
     - /Game/Mannequin/Animations/ThirdPersonIdle
     - /Game/Mannequin/Animations/ThirdPersonIdle.ThirdPersonIdle
     - AnimSequence'/Game/Mannequin/Animations/ThirdPersonIdle.ThirdPersonIdle'
- SlateDebugger.SlateDebuggerSubsystem: Debugs Slate at runtime. The navigation section records focus changes, navigation attempts
(with the hit-test candidates considered) and the input that caused them, so an agent can
explain why a widget received focus. Registered focus-context providers (CommonUI, for one)
add framework state to each focus record. The same recording can be opened in the Navigation
Logger editor tab. Load this when investigating focus or gamepad/keyboard navigation in PIE
or in editor UI. Widget lifetime debugging (constructed, destructed, rebuilt) lives in
UMGDebuggerSubsystem.
- LevelSequenceEditor.LevelSequenceEditorBlueprintLibrary: Level Sequence Editor Blueprint Library
- LevelSequenceEditor.LevelSequenceEditorSubsystem: ULevelSequenceEditorSubsystem
Subsystem for level sequence editor related utilities to scripts
- TemplateSequenceEditor.TemplateSequenceEditorSubsystem: Script access to template sequences and camera animation sequences, without needing them open in Sequencer.
- SequenceValidator.SequenceValidatorSubsystem: Script access to the Sequence Validator rules, which check sequences for common authoring mistakes such as
duplicate keys, sections a frame or two off notable times, sections on sub-frames, and missing assets or bindings.
- OptimusScripting.DeformerGraphScriptingSubsystem: Builds, edits, inspects and compiles Deformer Graph assets (UOptimusDeformer).

A deformer contains graphs (UpdateGraph always exists; SetupGraph and trigger graphs are optional),
variables, resources and component bindings. Graphs contain nodes linked through pins.

Graphs, nodes and pins are addressed by path:
- Graph: "UpdateGraph"
- Node:  "UpdateGraph/NodeName", where NodeName is the node's name, not its display name
- Pin:   "UpdateGraph/NodeName.PinName", sub-pins dot-separated, e.g. "UpdateGraph/MyKernel.Primary.Position"

Node types are "<Kind>/<Name>" identifiers from ListNodeTypes, e.g. "DataInterface/OptimusSkinnedMeshDataInterface".

Data domains: "" for a single value (parameter), "Vertex" for one value per vertex, "Vertex.Bone" for several
dimensions, "Vertex x 2" for a multiplier, "'Triangle * 3'" for an expression.

Every change is one undo step. Errors raise, with a message starting with "[Code:Argument]". Assets are not saved.

Every function is both PythonCallable and an MCP tool (AICallable), registered with the toolset registry when it is loaded.
- ControlRigEditor.ControlRigSequencerEditorLibrary: Helper functions to animate Control Rigs in level sequences from Python, Blueprints, and AI tools.

Invalid inputs, inaccessible or read-only assets, and failed operations raise a script error (a Python exception)
instead of returning a sentinel. A boolean that answers a question or reports whether anything changed (for example IsolateLinkedAnimTrack)
is a result, not an error. Most functions need the level sequence open in Sequencer, and some need Animation Mode active.
Frame parameters are display-rate frames unless TimeUnit is TickResolution.
Transform spaces: Local is the control's value (relative to its parent and offset), Global is Control Rig (component) space,
and World is world space.
The SetLocalControlRig* setters and SetControlRigWorldTransform(s) raise, without setting or keying anything, when the rig overrides
the value on evaluation (a control driven by rig logic, for example an FK control matched to IK). The check is one rig evaluation per
call. SetLocalControlRig* check in the rig's current pose, so only when the frame (the first frame for plural setters) is the current time;
SetControlRigWorldTransform(s) evaluate the sequence at the first frame first. Layered rigs, constrained controls and interactive drags are not checked.
